key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow can map the thermodynamic stability of complex hybrid perovskite alloys and show that stable regions are narrow, especially for Sn-based compositions.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a practical guide for compositional design of more stable perovskite solar absorbers, with the strongest stability found at high iodide content.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials trained on DFT data for fast structure relaxation
Secondary ML models predict energies directly from unrelaxed alloy structures
Free-energy landscapes computed across compositions, phases, disorder, and FA orientations
evidence_signal: The models were used to evaluate quaternary alloy phase stability across composition space for both Pb- and Sn-based (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3 systems.
watch_item: Because the approach relies on trained ML models and DFT-derived data, transferability beyond the sampled alloy space and phase space should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
